headline: CLI checks recovered; no broker repair warranted
summary: Both accounts returned exit 1 in scheduled keepalive rounds at 12:38:22 and 12:45:27 Eastern on October 13. Independent account-scoped metadata checks at 12:41 succeeded; the normal keepalive calls at 12:52:32/33 then succeeded and cleared this fault episode. The broker and keepalive stayed alive throughout the observed incident.
cause: A transient failure of the CLI metadata calls is established; its underlying cause is not retained in the sanitized generic error category. Exit 1 alone does not establish authorization expiry, a network failure, or a broker crash. Lock parsing agrees with the live unlocked state, deployed worker and keepalive hashes match source, signature verification succeeds, and the heartbeat advances.
resolution: No implementation change or activation is warranted by the verified checks. No broker or keepalive restart, auth wake, additional approval notification, or UI action was performed. Only incident evidence and documentation were added.
verification: 44 targeted Python tests passed across keepalive, recovery, isolated broker protocol, activation and agent guidance. The Node settlement, archive and dispatch test files returned exit 0. Absolute bin/op version and both account-scoped vault-list checks returned exit 0 with stdout and stderr discarded. Broker PID/session 1051 and /dev/ttys000, plus keepalive PID 1055, were preserved. Source/deployed hashes and running keepalive source hash match; bundle signature check returned 0. Timestamped lock parsing matches keepalive. Native readback verified the exact title, dotfiles cwd, Pinned section, strongest supported gpt-6-astra model and high effort. See artifacts/. Heartbeat advanced from 12:41:04 to 12:53:54 Eastern; final snapshot age was four seconds. Both keepalive account statuses are now ok, and fault_resolved records the exact incident episode at 12:52:33. Last successful prompted-call timestamps did not change.
activation: Existing installed code remains running; nothing is staged and no service load or user action is required for this recovered incident. Recovery continues to own scheduled checks and notification-click auth wakes. Future native authentication or macOS consent remains Taylor's action.
limitations: The exact reason for the brief generic CLI errors is not known and is not asserted. Successful metadata checks establish access at verification time, not future availability. No physical notification click or native consent UI was exercised. Archive scheduling is not archive completion; the helper must record its private readback receipt.
docs: Reviewed src/onepassword/README.md, agent-contract.md and autofixes/AGENTS.md. Updated README.md with this incident and the distinction between a successful manual smoke check and keepalive's stored account statuses. Existing shared contract already covers first-click release, quarantine, auth wake ownership and no-change settlement; no contract change or guidance sync was needed.
